stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: An ADC turns a continuous voltage into a discrete binary code. Sweep the input $V_{in}$ between $0$ and $V_{ref} = 5\,\text{V}$ and watch the 4-bit code jump one step at a time. Visit a LOW, a MID and a HIGH region to advance.
stages.concept: Uniform quantization with step $\text{LSB} = V_{ref}/2^n$. For $n = 4$ bits, $\text{LSB} = 5/16 \approx 0.3125\,\text{V}$. The output code is $\text{code} = \lfloor V_{in}/\text{LSB} \rfloor$ and the error $\varepsilon = V_{in} - \text{code}\cdot\text{LSB}$ is at most one LSB.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A sine wave is now fed to the ADC. Choose the number of bits $n$ so the staircase reconstruction (green) hugs the analogue target (orange) closely. Move to $n \geq 4$ to bring the reconstruction error under one visible tick.
stages.concept: Doubling $n$ halves the LSB and quarters the peak quantization error. Signal-to-noise ratio grows as $\text{SNR} \approx 6.02\,n + 1.76\,\text{dB}$: each extra bit buys about $6\,\text{dB}$ of fidelity.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: A 4-bit code is captured at the ADC output. Before touching anything, compute $V_{in} = \text{code}\cdot\text{LSB}$ on paper. Then pick the voltage band (LOW / MID / HIGH) it belongs to and press $\text{SUBMIT}$. Ace all three captures in one pass — a wrong pick reshuffles the deck.
stages.concept: Bands with $V_{ref} = 5\,\text{V}$: LOW $\in [0,\,1.25)\,\text{V}$ (codes 0000–0011), MID $\in [1.875,\,3.125)\,\text{V}$ (codes 0110–1001), HIGH $\in [3.75,\,5]\,\text{V}$ (codes 1100–1111). Convert the code to decimal, multiply by $\text{LSB} = 0.3125\,\text{V}$, look up the band.

labels.tip1: sweep V_in · visit low, mid and high regions
labels.tip2: raise n · the staircase snaps closer to the sine
labels.tip3: read the code · convert to V_in · pick the band
labels.peek_tip_1: LSB = V_ref / 2^n. Multiply the decimal code by the LSB to recover V_in.
labels.peek_tip_2: For 4 bits the range 0..15 splits into thirds: bottom quarter is LOW, middle is MID, top quarter is HIGH.

1.1: Move the slider slowly — the code stays the same for a whole LSB-wide band of V_in.
1.2: One LSB is V_ref / 2^n = 5/16 ≈ 0.3125 V. That is how wide each step is.
1.3: Visit V_in < 1.25 V (LOW), V_in in [1.875, 3.125] V (MID), and V_in > 3.75 V (HIGH).

2.1: The staircase (green) is what the ADC actually reconstructs. The smooth sine (orange) is the ideal.
2.2: Each extra bit halves the LSB and doubles the number of staircase steps per period.
2.3: n = 2 gives 4 steps — a coarse blocky shape. n = 4 gives 16 steps — the shape starts to look like a sine.

3.1: Convert the 4-bit code to decimal. code = b3·8 + b2·4 + b1·2 + b0.
3.2: Multiply that decimal by LSB = 0.3125 V. The result is the lower edge of the V_in bucket.
3.3: Compare with band edges: LOW < 1.25 V, MID between 1.875 V and 3.125 V, HIGH > 3.75 V.
